title: SDK snippet parity across Python/TypeScript/Go (auth, retries/timeouts, streaming) for guided onboarding
creator: Monica Patel
description:
Goal
Ensure the code snippets linked from the Console guided onboarding checklist are consistent across Python/TypeScript/Go and match the checklist step expectations. This is specifically about snippets for:
1) Auth (API key + base URL)
2) Retries + timeouts (production defaults + explicit configuration)
3) Streaming (stable stream loop, disconnect handling guidance)

Why
We’re seeing onboarding drop-offs caused by snippet drift:
- Different env var names and client init patterns across SDKs
- Retry/timeout guidance varies (some snippets show none, some show aggressive retries)
- Streaming examples differ materially (event names, loop patterns, disconnect handling)

This ticket aligns the “canonical snippet contract” so:
- Docs and Console checklist deep-links can point at one recommended pattern per step
- Checklist validation expectations remain truthful (e.g., step says “set retries/timeouts” but snippet does not)
- Support can rely on a consistent baseline when troubleshooting (401/429/stream disconnect)

Non-goals
- Adding brand new SDK surface area beyond what’s needed to make snippets consistent (track follow-ups separately)
- Dedicated/Private onboarding (Phase 1 Hosted API only)

Decisions / conventions (final)
Auth
- Env var: REDWOOD_API_KEY (all SDKs)
- Optional env var: REDWOOD_BASE_URL (for proxy/dev; default remains hosted)
- Snippets must show a single client initialization line and an example request.

Retries/timeouts
- Snippets must:
  - Use SDK defaults if they are “production-safe” (bounded retries + exponential backoff + jitter)
  - Also include an explicit configuration example showing how to set max_retries and timeout in each SDK
  - Mention handling of 429 with respect to Retry-After (where supported)
- Terminology alignment: “timeout” refers to overall request timeout; avoid mixing connect/read timeouts in onboarding snippets.

Streaming
- Snippets must:
  - Demonstrate incremental token consumption
  - Show a safe termination condition
  - Include a short note on recommended behavior for disconnects (retry creating a new stream, do not assume resume)
- Keep the streaming example minimal; avoid tool-calling + streaming in the same snippet for Phase 1.

Checklist mapping
- These snippets are the ones linked from the Console steps:
  - “Make your first request” -> auth snippet + minimal non-streaming request
  - “Enable retries & timeouts” -> retries/timeouts snippet + short rationale
  - “Try streaming” -> streaming snippet + disconnect guidance

Implementation plan
1) Audit current snippets in docs + quickstarts for the three SDKs; document drift and choose the canonical pattern.
2) Land SDK changes required to support the canonical pattern (defaults + naming consistency where feasible).
3) Update docs snippets and ensure they compile/run (at least smoke-tested locally; ideally in CI).
4) Confirm Console checklist copy matches the actual snippet behaviors (esp. retries/timeouts wording).

Risks / notes
- Go SDK currently exposes timeout configuration differently than Python/TS; we’ll align snippet usage first, then consider deeper API parity as a follow-up.
- Streaming disconnect handling differs by runtime; keep the guidance consistent and conservative.

Follow-ups (not in scope here)
- Add automated snippet compilation tests wired to docs build for all SDKs (propose separate ENG ticket once we see how docs repo wants to enforce)
- Structured output snippet parity (Phase 2 checklist step; track when the checklist adds it)
acceptance_criteria:
1) Docs snippets for Python/TS/Go use the same env var naming (REDWOOD_API_KEY) and the same conceptual client initialization pattern.
2) Each SDK has a retries/timeouts snippet that:
   - Uses bounded retries and a request timeout
   - Clearly shows how to configure max_retries and timeout
3) Each SDK has a streaming snippet that:
   - Streams tokens incrementally
   - Includes a short, consistent note on disconnect handling
4) Docs PR is merged updating snippets and references used by guided onboarding; SDK PRs merged if needed to support the snippet contract.
5) DevEx + Docs sign off that snippets match checklist step wording (no misleading claims).
